note: One-beat content. A line is read and closed; it asks nothing and records nothing. Two-beat jokes with a setup and a punchline stay as chapters, because a punchline needs its own page. Append freely: there are no cooldowns, so the pool only gets better.

lines.text: Most of a life is spent on days nobody would write down.
Nothing important ever felt urgent while it was happening.
The habit you keep badly still counts.
You cannot change a day you did not notice.
Beginning again is not starting over.
The thing you do without counting it is usually the thing holding.
An honest sentence about a bad day is worth more than a good one about nothing.
Later is a place people keep things they do not want to decide about.
Small and repeated beats large and once. It is not close.
Rest is not the reward for the work. It is part of it.
Nobody is grading this.
What you did is evidence. What you meant to do is not.
A mood is weather. It tells you about today, not about you.
You are allowed to have done enough for one day.
Coming back is the whole skill. Everything else is detail.
My sleep schedule is less a schedule and more a rumour.
I have a great relationship with tomorrow. We have never met.
Drank a glass of water. Considering a parade.
I was productive today in the sense that time passed.
Wrote a list. The list is now the achievement.
My gym membership is a subscription to guilt with a locker attached.
I am a morning person. The morning just starts at one.
Inbox zero is a myth told to children.
I bought a plant to prove I can keep something alive. The plant is nervous.
I can do two things at once, badly, simultaneously.
I give excellent advice. I take none of it.
Picked up my phone to check one thing. See you in an hour.
I cook in two modes: from scratch, and from desperation.
A nap is just a save point.
I have laser focus. The laser is pointed at nothing in particular.
Honey does not spoil.
lines.sub: Jars found in ancient tombs were still edible.

lines.text: An octopus has three hearts.
lines.sub: Two pump to the gills. One pumps to the rest of it.

lines.text: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
lines.sub: It turns slower than it orbits.

lines.text: Sharks are older than trees.
lines.sub: By roughly a hundred million years.

lines.text: Cleopatra lived closer to the moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Sea otters hold hands while they sleep.
lines.sub: So they do not drift apart.

lines.text: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy.
lines.sub: Around three trillion, against a few hundred billion.

lines.text: The Eiffel Tower is taller in summer.
lines.sub: The iron expands in the heat, by about fifteen centimetres.

lines.text: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings.
lines.sub: Cubes do not roll away, which is the point.

lines.text: A banana is a berry. A strawberry is not.
lines.sub: Botany does not care what we call things.

lines.text: Most of the oxygen you breathe came from the ocean, not from forests.
You are slightly taller in the morning.
lines.sub: Your spine compresses through the day.

lines.text: You had around three hundred bones as a baby and have around two hundred and six now.
A cloud can weigh hundreds of tonnes.
lines.sub: It floats because the air beneath it is heavier still.

lines.text: Your sense of taste is mostly smell.
lines.sub: Hold your nose and an apple and an onion get harder to tell apart.
